verdict_text: NO. The plan loads `base`, `ft1`, and `ft2` as three separate providers but never deletes the `ft1::` and `ft2::` tensor namespaces before writing output — it only removes the intermediate `.tv1`/`.tv2` tensors it created under `base::`. Since the engine's state after transforms carries all still-present tensors from every provider into `save_output`, the written file would contain the base's 244 tensors plus all 244 `ft1` tensors plus all 244 `ft2` tensors (732 total), not the required 244, violating Required-result clause 4 ("a single file ... with exactly 244 tensors"). The final `assert: { count: { of: 'base::.*', is: 244 } }` only checks the `base::` partition and would pass even though the actual output is wrong, so it fails to satisfy the "output has exactly 244 tensors" required check as well.
